description: Figure 2 is a concentric circular diagram illustrating a hierarchical taxonomy of medical ethics, as described in its caption. The innermost circle contains four distinct segments, each representing one of the four pillar principles in medicine. Surrounding this inner circle is a larger outer ring divided into twenty-six segments, which visually represent the 26 categories derived from clustering the 256 detailed principles. The diagram uses this layered structure to show the relationship between the broad principles and the more specific categories. There are no color distinctions, percentage labels, or legends visible within the figure itself; it relies purely on the spatial arrangement of the segments to convey its hierarchical organization. The segments appear to be arranged in a clockwise order around each circle, though their specific labels are not readable in the provided image.
